posts.name: Greg Harrington
posts.cooked:
Where does the bug appear (feature/product)?

Somewhere else…

Describe the Bug

Grok Bot desktop on macOS loses the Mac local-computer link after the app has been healthy. This is not a permissions / Always-allow issue.

The Mac is reached only through a detached local-exec daemon:

/Applications/Grok Bot.app/Contents/MacOS/Grok Bot
/Applications/Grok Bot.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar/dist/local-exec-daemon/main.cjs

That process registers as a local-exec provider and must send ping heartbeats. Host liveness window is 30 seconds (SAND_LOCAL_EXEC_LIVENESS_WINDOW_MS = 30000). There is no user-facing keep-alive or auto-respawn. Leftover daemon processes after a crash block a clean respawn. Agents cannot recover this themselves because ExternalShell is that dead channel.

Failure sequence (same session):

  1. Stale heartbeat while the provider is still registered: Your computer “anonymous” is unavailable ‚Äî it looks disconnected.
  2. Then no providers: Your local machine isn’t connected right now (the Grok Bot desktop app must be open and online to run commands on it).

The computer id/label shown is “anonymous”. Cloud Agent Computer (the shared box) keeps working. Cursor IDE is fine. This is only the Grok Bot Mac local-exec link.

Observed on 16 Aug 2026 (WITA / UTC+8), Grok Bot 0.20.0, leftover 0.16.0 crashpad still running from an older install:

  • 2:08pm: daemon pid 67049 started; stayed up ~80 min
  • 3:31pm: stale heartbeat (anonymous); 3:37pm no provider
  • Later relaunches: pid 71938 (died within a minute), 72164 (dropped ~14 min), 72817 (5:14pm)
  • 5:35pm stale heartbeat on 72817, then recovered without relaunch at 5:37pm (same pid) ‚Äî heartbeat can miss and come back
  • 6:10pm stale again on the same pid

A Mac reboot only cleans leftover daemons / old crashpad / hung Electron. It does not stop the 30s heartbeat miss.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open Grok Bot desktop 0.20.0 on macOS and leave it running (do not Cmd+Q).
  2. Confirm the Mac is reachable from a Grok Bot agent (trivial local command succeeds). Confirm a local-exec-daemon process is up:
    ps aux | grep local-exec-daemon
  3. Leave the app in the foreground or background. Do not change Always-allow / local execution settings.
  4. Wait. In this case the first healthy run lasted ~80 minutes, then a 30-second heartbeat miss.
  5. Agent calls to the Mac then fail with: Your computer “anonymous” is unavailable ‚Äî it looks disconnected.
  6. Shortly after, the daemon is gone and the error becomes: Your local machine isn’t connected right now (the Grok Bot desktop app must be open and online to run commands on it).
  7. Relaunching the app without killing leftover local-exec-daemon processes often fails to restore the link. Workaround that works:
    osascript -e ‘tell application “Grok Bot” to quit’; sleep 2; pkill -f ‘local-exec-daemon’; sleep 1; open -a “Grok Bot”

Expected Behavior

While Grok Bot desktop is open and online, the local-exec-daemon should keep heartbeating (or auto-respawn) so the Mac stays reachable. A missed ping should not permanently drop the machine or require the user to kill leftover processes by hand. The computer should have a real name, not “anonymous”.

Operating System

MacOS

Version Information

Grok Bot desktop 0.20.0 (stable), macOS.
App path: /Applications/Grok Bot.app
Also observed a leftover 0.16.0 crashpad handler still running from a prior install.
This is Grok Bot desktop, not Cursor IDE / CLI / iOS. Product dropdown has no Grok Bot option, so this is filed as Somewhere else.

For AI issues: which model did you use?

N/A ‚Äî not a model/chat issue. Local-exec daemon / Mac connection.

For AI issues: add Request ID with privacy disabled

N/A. Host error class seen: SAND-E0608 (desktopLocalExecSpawnFailed). No public Request ID. In-app Cursor feedback for the same bug was already submitted 16 Aug 2026 (no public URL).

Additional Information

Not a duplicate of:

  • Grok Bot ExternalShell blocked despite Always allow (permissions / Always-allow; staff workaround mentions killing local-exec-daemon leftovers, but the bug there is UNAPPROVED ExternalShell, not a later heartbeat miss)
  • Grok Bot issues - who can help? (cloud setup / “Can’t reach your computer” / NXDOMAIN ‚Äî the Agent Computer, not the Mac daemon)
  • Higgsfield MCP 30‚Äì60s disconnect (plugin session, not local-exec)

Forum search for local-exec-daemon only hits Mohit’s workaround on the Always-allow thread. No existing report of a live daemon that later misses its 30s ping, labels the Mac “anonymous”, then vanishes until leftovers are killed.

Official docs only treat local-computer failures as a permission setting. Agents cannot restart the desktop app remotely while the link is down.

Does this stop you from using Cursor

Sometimes - I can sometimes use Cursor

posts.name: Maaz Kazi
posts.cooked:
Same failure on 0.44.0 (Stable, “You’re up to date”), macOS 26.6, Mac mini — but the leftover-process workaround in this thread does not apply here, because the helper is healthy and connected and the assistant still cannot reach the machine.

What the app reports. The helper restarts in a loop, each instance killed immediately after start:

[sand-local-exec-daemon] started (pid 11047); serving local exec over the gateway
    [sand-local-exec-daemon] received SIGTERM, shutting down {"error":"cli_unknown_command"}
    [sand-local-exec-daemon] started (pid 11222); serving local exec over the gateway
    [sand-local-exec-daemon] received SIGTERM, shutting down {"error":"cli_unknown_command"}
    ... repeats for pids 11305, 11318, 11419 ...

A 401 against the gateway was also reported before a reboot.

The cli_unknown_command seems worth attention: the app bundle ships no cursor or sand CLI binary (only cursor_proclist.node), and there is no cursor/sand/grok executable anywhere on PATH. So nothing local can be shadowing or answering that command.

**Ruled out on this machine.** Each checked directly rather than assumed:

* Full Disk Access — granted (kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles, auth 2, in the system TCC database)
* Code signature — valid and unmodified, Developer ID Anysphere (DCNK4UB866)
* App location — /Applications, not translocated or quarantined
* Settings > Computer > Execution — Always allow
* Settings > Computer > Current computer — matches hostname exactly
* Conflicting CLI on PATH — none
* macOS firewall — disabled
* Proxy / PAC — none configured
* VPN interception — a VPN client is installed but not routing; default route is the ordinary LAN
* MTU — 1472-byte payloads pass, so no fragmentation black hole
* DNS — clean, no interception
* Endpoints — api2.cursor.sh 200, cursor.com 200, api.cursor.com 200

**Current state.** After a reboot the helper stopped flapping: one process, stable for 17+ minutes, holding an established TLS connection to the gateway, with crashSeen false in sand-session-marker.json. It is healthy and connected, and the assistant still reports it cannot see the machine — so this looks like a registration or authorisation failure at the gateway rather than local process cleanup.

Separately, attaching a 12 kB .md file and sending it fails with a network error, while ordinary chat messages send fine over the same connection.

Three questions that would help:

1. What does cli_unknown_command correspond to server-side on 0.44.0?
2. Does the 401 mean the daemon's registration token is rejected independently of the app session, which is signed in and working?
3. Is the attachment upload failure the same authorisation path?

Happy to supply more detail if useful.

posts.name: Colin
posts.cooked:
Hey @Maaz_Kazi, thanks for the detailed report, and you were right to rule out the local side. Your helper is connected fine on our end. What is out of date is Grok Bot’s cloud computer: it came back up on an older internal build that does not know how to see the helper, so the assistant keeps reporting your Mac as unavailable even though everything on the Mac is healthy. Attaching files fails for the same reason, since that older build does not understand how the current app uploads them.

The fix is on the cloud side and takes a minute:

  1. In Grok Bot, open Settings, then Updates.
  2. Click “Update Grok Bot’s Computer” and wait for it to finish (your bots, files, and logins are kept).
  3. Send your bot a quick test like “run hostname on my Mac”, and try the .md attachment again.
